correctness.rationale: PASS: For 0<a<2, a double stationary root would require a²=4(1+3cos²2t)>=4; hence four simple alternating roots persist. The derivative's unit-circle quartic P(z)=2z⁴+ae^{iφ}z³-ae^{-iφ}z-2 has vanishing z² coefficient and root product -1. Equating the positive and negative derivative arc-lengths forces the products of alternating roots to have opposite phase and then an antipodal pair, leading algebraically to φ in (π/2)Z. The reverse zero case follows from reflection; implicit differentiation at a=0 yields R-π=(a²/8)sin2φ+O(a⁴). Continuity and absence of any other zero extends the sign to all a in (0,2). Direct integration of the resonant cubic term gives -3a²sin2φ/2. At φ=π/4 the quadratic equation in sin(t+π/4) yields R=2(asin((sqrt(a²+32)-a)/8)+asin((sqrt(a²+32)+a)/8)); expansions as a↑2 yield π/3-(2/√3)√(2-a)+O(2-a). The boundary a=2 is excluded from four-extrema claim. Independent freshly coded root-bracketing plus numeric quadrature checked 28 (a,φ) sign cases and four closed-form phase cases; these finite checks are not the global proof.
